diagnosis.summary: All four services are under a sharp traffic surge, with request rates between 7.8x and 34x their baselines. Payment-service is returning 5xx errors on 100% of requests, and order-service is returning 5xx errors on 65% of requests. Both services also show p95 latency roughly 70 to 390 times their baselines.
diagnosis.root_cause: A traffic surge across all services and a complete payment-service failure, active at the same time, are the most likely concurrent root causes.
evidence: Request rates surged across every service: product-service rose from 14.98 to 117.18 rps (7.8x), cart-service from 2.05 to 25.95 rps (12.7x), order-service from 2.97 to 49.43 rps (16.6x), and payment-service from 0.94 to 32.13 rps (34x).
Payment-service 5xx error rate is now 100% against a baseline of 0, and its p95 latency rose from 4.5 ms to 1,756.3 ms, a 390x increase.
Order-service 5xx error rate is now 65% against a baseline of 0, and its p95 latency rose from 25.1 ms to 1,785.8 ms, a 71x increase.
Order-service dependency errors to payment-service reached 1,928 per minute from a baseline of 0, and the dependency p95 latency rose from 22.1 ms to 2,159.6 ms, a 98x increase.
recommended_actions: Investigate payment-service Lambda logs and concurrency immediately, as it is returning 5xx errors on every request and is the most user-visible fault; reduce or restore its ability to handle the current 32.13 rps load.
Apply rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage to cap incoming traffic toward the pre-surge baseline while the payment-service fault is being resolved.
Check Lambda throttle counts on all four services, since the account-wide Lambda concurrency pool is shared and the traffic surge across all services may be exhausting it.
After payment-service errors are resolved, recheck order-service 5xx rate and p95 latency to confirm recovery, then address any remaining order-service issues separately.
Record the timestamps at which each signal changes as fixes are applied, so the effect of each individual action can be distinguished.
